headline: Quieter buttons, and a version list you can hide
notes: **The version list can be put away.** Settings → Options → *Show version history*. On by default; turn it off and the list at the foot of the panel goes, giving that height back to the buttons. Nothing is forgotten — the panel keeps its record and the switch brings it straight back

**The buttons look quieter.** The face is now darker than the panel rather than lighter, so a button reads as cut into the surface instead of sitting on it, and the line around it is a line rather than a frame
**Your email address is no longer printed in the panel.** The licence line says Active and which machine you are on, and nothing else — so a screenshot of VersionUp never carries your address
**The machine count comes from the product, not from your key.** A key issued before the two-machine limit was settled could show the wrong number; it now always shows the right one
**The buttons say what they do.** Version up and Approve now carry their names under the symbol, the way Project always has. Previously Project was the only button nobody had to guess at

**A narrow dock gets bars, not squares.** Squeeze the panel below about 200px and the three buttons become full-width bars with their names beside the symbol; squeeze further and the words step aside, all three together rather than one at a time. That used to start at 170px — narrower than the panel would let itself be dragged, so most people never saw it

**Any button can be hidden, Version up included.** Turn off what you do not use and the panel reshapes around what is left — no empty band where a button used to be. The last one on cannot be switched off, because a panel with no buttons has no obvious way back

**A list of your versions**, at the foot of the panel and closed until you open it. Sequence and Project tabs, the name and when it was made, and a green tick on any cut that was approved. Clicking a project row opens its folder
The panel only lists versions it made itself. Anything you renamed by hand reads as no record rather than pretending to remember it
**Alt-click Project** to branch the project file the same way Alt branches a sequence, and **Shift-click** for a new major. **Cmd-click** shows the current project in the Finder
**Name your project versions your own way** — a pattern with date, time, client, project and initials in it, or one of six ready-made presets
**VersionUp will no longer save over a project that already exists.** Saving a project cannot be undone, so a click that would land on a file already on disk is stopped instead
**You can see when it is busy.** The button dims and reads WORKING while Premiere saves. It does not animate, because Premiere stops the panel dead while it works — a spinner would be a lie
**The settings sheet has been rebuilt**: one column, no boxes, grey headings and a symbol on every row, and a visual picker for choosing which buttons you want

**Feedback has a third option: Testimonial.** If VersionUp has saved you something, you can say so, tell me who to credit, and tick whether I may quote you on the website. Nothing is ever quoted without that tick
**The buttons' corners now fit their shape.** Squeeze the panel and they tighten; give it room and they soften — so a squashed dock no longer turns them into lozenges
**Save, Send, Activate and Close are the right colour now.** They were still Adobe's blue while the rest of the panel had moved to violet
The three menu items that open a window you fill in now say so, with a trailing "…"
The accent colour is now violet rather than Adobe blue. White text on the old blue fell below the accessibility standard for normal text; the violet clears it
